author: riverlijunjie
title: Windows GPU unit tests job fails extracting OpenVINO packages due to locked tbb12.dll
signature: windows runner extract openvino packages expand-archive remove-item access to the path denied unauthorizedaccessexception locked dll file|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: GPU unit tests
failed_jobs.symptom: Extract OpenVINO packages step fails: Remove-Item cannot delete tbb12.dll, Access to the path is denied

key_errors:
Remove-Item : Cannot remove item C:\actions-runner\_work\openvino\openvino\install\runtime\3rdparty\tbb\bin\tbb12.dll:
Access to the path 'C:\actions-runner\_work\openvino\openvino\install\runtime\3rdparty\tbb\bin\tbb12.dll' is denied.
At C:\Windows\system32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\Modules\Microsoft.PowerShell.Archive\Microsoft.PowerShell.Archive.psm1:1029
+ CategoryInfo          : PermissionDenied: (...tbb\bin\tbb12.dll:FileInfo) [Remove-Item], UnauthorizedAccessException
+ FullyQualifiedErrorId : RemoveFileSystemItemUnAuthorizedAccess,Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.RemoveItemCommand
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
root_cause: Expand-Archive -Force on Windows tries to delete tbb12.dll before overwriting it, but the DLL is still locked/held open by another process (likely a lingering process from a prior step on the same self-hosted runner, e.g. antivirus scanning or a previous test run that did not release the handle), causing Remove-Item to throw UnauthorizedAccessException and the step to fail with exit code 1. This is a recurring, runner-state-dependent infrastructure issue, not caused by this commit's code changes (a GPU fusion-ops PR unrelated to packaging/CI scripts).
reproduction_steps: N/A - requires a Windows self-hosted runner where a prior process still holds a handle on install/runtime/3rdparty/tbb/bin/tbb12.dll; cannot be reliably reproduced locally. To reproduce conditions: on Windows, open/lock install\runtime\3rdparty\tbb\bin\tbb12.dll in another process, then run Expand-Archive -Force against an existing install directory containing that file.
recommended_actions: Ensure prior steps/processes on the runner (e.g., previous test binaries, antivirus/indexing) fully release handles on install/ before the Extract OpenVINO packages step runs; add an explicit process cleanup or short retry/backoff before Expand-Archive.
Wrap the Expand-Archive call in a PowerShell retry loop (e.g., 3-5 attempts with delay) to tolerate transient file locks, as this signature has recurred 7 times in 24h.
Consider extracting to a fresh/clean directory instead of overwriting an existing install/ directory with -Force, avoiding the Remove-Item-on-locked-file path entirely.

Escalate to the runner pool maintainers: this is the 7th occurrence of the same locked-tbb12.dll failure in ~24 hours across unrelated commits, suggesting a systemic runner/antivirus issue rather than isolated flakiness.
prevention_strategies: Add retry-with-backoff around Expand-Archive/Remove-Item on Windows runners, or extract into a clean target directory to avoid overwrite-triggered deletes of potentially-locked DLLs. Track repeated occurrences of this signature and proactively investigate runner health (antivirus, leftover processes) once the pattern count crosses a threshold (e.g., >5 in 24h).
historical_context: This exact signature (514ffa2ab52ad344) has now been recorded 8 times since 2026-11-09T16:30:00Z, most recently at 2026-11-10T18:01:09Z, always on the 'GPU unit tests' job of Windows post-commit runs, across many unrelated commits - strongly indicating a systemic Windows runner infrastructure issue (locked tbb12.dll) rather than a one-off flake.
